source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 19 April 1924, p. 5 ("Tyrone Local Government Elections")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: image-read (BNA article image, 19 Apr 1924 p5 art 86): the nominations closed on Tuesday [15 April 1924], received at Omagh 'and also by the clerks of the Urban Councils for their local divisions'; 'The full list of those returned is as follows', in which Cookstown and Dungannon appear between Coalisland and Donaghmore. A separate paragraph headed 'County Councillor' adds that for Cookstown Division 'the nominations were John Glasgow, J.P., retiring Councillor'.

note: Nominations closed Tuesday 15 April 1924 for the election fixed for 28 May 1924. The two urban county divisions, Cookstown and Dungannon, were nominated before the clerks of those urban councils rather than at Omagh, which is why the Ulster Herald and Belfast News-Letter lists (the Freeman's Journal, 16 April 1924, p. 5, BNA OCR only, says the county council nominations for Cookstown and Dungannon Urban 'will be lodged at these centres') omit them. The Mid-Ulster Mail of 19 April 1924, p. 5, prints the full list of those returned unopposed including Cookstown (John Glasgow, J.P.) and Dungannon (Joseph Newell). With these two the round has 21 members returned plus the six divisions with no nomination (Ballygawley, Carrickmore, Coagh, Dromore, Plumbridge, Pomeroy), 27 in all. Returned unopposed (printed 'Dungannon—Joseph Newell.' in the list of those returned). Returned unopposed again in 1927 (Belfast Telegraph, 21 April 1927, p. 10).
